region2_forecast: Metro Manila, Ilocos Region, Cordillera Administrative Region, Cagayan Valley, CALABARZON, MIMAROPA, the rest of Central Luzon, and Antique
Metro Manila, Ilocos Region, Cordillera Administrative Region, Cagayan Valley, western section of CALABARZON, and western section of MIMAROPA

Ilocos Region, Cagayan, Isabela, Cordillera Administrative Region, Central Luzon, National Capital Region, most areas of CALABARZON, MIMAROPA except Puerto Princesa, Western part of Panay, Negros Occidental, Southern Leyte, Zamboanga del Norte, Bukidnon, Davao del Norte, Davao del Sur, Surigao del Norte, Surigao del Sur, and Lanao del Sur
Rest of Cagayan Valley, Alabat, Mulanay, most of Bicol Region, Eastern part of Panay, Samar, Eastern Samar, General Santos City, rest of Caraga, and rest of BARMM

Moderate El Niño is present in the Tropical Pacific. Climate models predict that El Niño will continue until the first half of 2027 and may reach a very strong state before the end of 2026. El Niño increases the likelihood of below-normal rainfall, which may lead to adverse impacts, including dry spells and droughts in some areas of the country. However, over the western part of the country, above-normal rainfall conditions during the Southwest monsoon season (i.e., Habagat) may also occur.
